# AgenticPipeline Report

I first loaded the dataset using `load_dataset_tool` (`load_dataset_9`), which contained 2,257 documents across four categories: `alt.atheism` (480), `comp.graphics` (584), `sci.med` (594), and `soc.religion.christian` (599). I inspected the dataset using `inspect_data_tool` (`inspect_data_14`) and checked for missing values (`check_missing_15`) and duplicates (`check_duplicates_16`). Neither missing values nor duplicate documents were found. I also analyzed document lengths using `describe_data_tool` (`describe_data_17`). The average document length was approximately 1,993 characters, while the maximum reached 60,713 characters, indicating substantial variation in document length.

![Document length distribution](../plots/韋妍伃_agentic-pipeline_plot_describe_data_17.png)

Next, I constructed a Document-Term Matrix (DTM) using `build_dtm_tool` (`dtm_18`), containing 2,257 documents and 35,788 unique terms. The matrix had a sparsity of 99.547%, meaning that most terms were absent from most documents. Term frequency analysis (`term_freq_19`) showed that common words such as "the" (29,825), "and" (13,017), and "is" (12,343) appeared frequently. The DTM heatmap (`dtm_heatmap_20`) further illustrated the sparse structure. I then applied variance filtering with a threshold of 0.01 (`variance_filter_11`), reducing the number of features from 35,788 to 5,354. This removed many low-variance features while retaining terms with greater variation across documents.

![DTM heatmap](../plots/韋妍伃_agentic-pipeline_plot_dtm_heatmap_20.png)

I also applied Pearson correlation filtering with a threshold of 0.15 for each category. The results retained 68 features for `soc.religion.christian` (`pearson_filter_4`), 63 for `sci.med` (`pearson_filter_5`), 55 for `comp.graphics` (`pearson_filter_6`), and 111 for `alt.atheism` (`pearson_filter_7`). Some selected terms were closely related to their categories, such as "church" and "bible" for Christianity, "medical" and "patient" for medicine, and "graphics" and "animation" for computer graphics. However, other selected features were associated with message headers or author information rather than actual topics. I further examined the 20 highest-variance terms using `feature_correlation_matrix_tool` (`feature_corr_10`). Strong positive correlations between common terms, such as "the" and "of" (0.9442), suggested that some features contained overlapping information.

![Feature correlation matrix](../plots/韋妍伃_agentic-pipeline_plot_feature_corr_10.png)

For pattern mining, I used the FP-Growth algorithm with a minimum support count of 14 and variance-based filtering. The analysis identified 8,635 frequent patterns in `alt.atheism` (`mine_patterns_12`) and 10,609 patterns in `soc.religion.christian` (`mine_patterns_13`). For example, the pattern containing "lines" and "organization" appeared in 453 `alt.atheism` documents, while "lines" appeared in all 599 `soc.religion.christian` documents. Although many frequent patterns were discovered, highly frequent terms such as "lines" and "organization" were likely related to document metadata rather than meaningful semantic relationships. This suggests that additional text preprocessing could improve the interpretability of the discovered patterns.

Finally, I explored dimensionality reduction and document similarity. PCA (`reduce_dims_24`) reduced the document representations to two dimensions, with the first principal component explaining 65.94% of the variance and the second explaining 4.33%, giving a combined explained variance of 70.27%. This indicates that most of the variance captured by these two components came from the first principal component. I also applied t-SNE (`reduce_dims_25`, random state = 1) to obtain a nonlinear two-dimensional representation for exploring local document relationships. However, the numerical results alone do not establish whether the four categories form clearly separated clusters. Additionally, I converted the category labels into one-hot encoded vectors (`binarize_labels_26`) and calculated the cosine similarity between documents at indices 1 and 2 (`cosine_sim_27`), obtaining a value of 0.4558. Document 1 belongs to `comp.graphics`, while Document 2 belongs to `soc.religion.christian`. Although these documents belong to different categories, they still exhibit a moderate degree of similarity in their term representations. This suggests that documents from different topics may share common vocabulary or textual structures, and cosine similarity alone may not fully reflect their semantic differences. 

![PCA visualization](../plots/韋妍伃_agentic-pipeline_plot_reduce_dims_24.png)

![t-SNE visualization](../plots/韋妍伃_agentic-pipeline_plot_reduce_dims_25.png)
